The official annotated tag was unsigned according to the GitHub API. The SHA256
pins the downloaded archive, not an independently authenticated release signature.
The small mfem-4.10-pin.json is the machine-readable provenance record.

License:BSD3-Clause. Retain licenses/mfem-4.10/LICENSE and NOTICE with redistributed
backend binaries. This serial configuration needs no Hypre/Metis/MPI dependency.

Windows native GCC build used the existing C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/g++.exe and
project-local CMake/Ninja tools. No global MSYS2 packages were modified.

Configure from the project root (substitute full tool and destination paths):
cmake -S third-party/mfem-source-4.10 -B third-party/mfem-build -G Ninja
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/g++.exe
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=<project>/third-party/mfem-sdk
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON
  -DMFEM_USE_MPI=OFF -DMFEM_USE_METIS=OFF -DMFEM_USE_LAPACK=OFF
  -DMFEM_USE_EXCEPTIONS=ON -DMFEM_THREAD_SAFE=ON -DMFEM_USE_MEMALLOC=OFF
  -DMFEM_USE_OPENMP=OFF -DMFEM_USE_LEGACY_OPENMP=OFF
  -DMFEM_ENABLE_TESTING=OFF -DMFEM_ENABLE_EXAMPLES=OFF -DMFEM_ENABLE_MINIAPPS=OFF
cmake --build third-party/mfem-build --target install -j2

The Studio DLL statically links installed mfem (MFEMConfig.cmake target mfem).
MFEM_USE_EXCEPTIONS is mandatory and checked by the wrapper at compile time.
The SDK has MFEM_THREAD_SAFE enabled, but all Studio MFEM invocations are also
serialized, after taking the shared CPU reservation. No outer concurrent MFEM
execution, private OpenMP pool or distributed solver is claimed. Actual Linux
native FEM/Qt/PETSc probes have executed in the dedicated QA VM; the coherent
final refreshed platform acceptance is tracked in HANDOFF/status logs, rather
than inferred from this build recipe. High-order systems/transient/adaptive and
mixed-order weak-flux interfaces have separate current FEM specifications.

The upstream library emits a NOMINMAX redefinition warning in general/tic_toc.cpp
with this GCC Windows configuration. Studio wrapper sources compile with warnings
enabled and treat the upstream SDK headers as SYSTEM; no warning flags were muted
for Studio source. Build and numerical evidence live in the task verification logs.

IMPLEMENTED OPTIONAL PETSC BACKEND
The project-local Windows PETSc3.25.1 real sequential SDK and Linux PETSc>=3.25
adapter support petscsolve KSP GMRES/CG and petscroot SNES with cached native
residuals/compiler-generated Jacobians. Shell CSR actions use Studio's shared
CPU grants; AIJ/ILU and PETSc bookkeeping remain sequential. Original residuals
are checked before success; no interpreted solver callback is substituted.
See specs/petsc_v0_2.txt, examples/native-petsc/, third-party/petsc-sdk/README.txt
and third-party/build-petsc-linux.sh.
Windows and Linux native probes have executed; the latest coherent full build,
numerical/graphics/relocation acceptance remains subject to final coordinator
logs. PETSc is a linear/nonlinear algebra backend, not a replacement for MFEM's
spaces/meshes/integrators. MPI/distributed PETSc or MFEM is not implemented here.
Retain PETSc's BSD2-Clause licence and dependency notices when distributing it.
